title: Don't just slap on a chatbot: building AI that works before you ask

summary: Arthur Objartel opens by critiquing the current trend of simply adding chatbot interfaces to products without considering whether this actually helps users. As a product designer at Evil Martians, he shares lessons from building Tegon, an AI-powered issue tracker, where he took the opposite approach: proactive AI that doesn't wait to be asked. He references Clippy from MS Word as having the right concept 25 years too early, arguing that modern technology can now realize that vision properly. He demonstrates three modes of proactive AI. Suggestion mode tracks what users write in real time and asks specific, contextual questions at the right moment—such as when someone reports a bug. Action mode identifies when an issue can be split into sub-issues and suggests better organization based on previous data and domain understanding. Question+action mode combines these, thinking about timelines and resources like a good project manager. All of this happens within the natural flow of work—no context switching, no extra windows, no chat interfaces. Users retain control and can revert changes with one click. He outlines three rules: AI should supplement user agency not replace it, offer recommendations never force them, and be part of the natural workflow not stop it. He extends the pattern to code editors, design tools, and communication tools. He closes with practical guidance: find friction points where users stop to ask for help, identify behavioral patterns where users need assistance, and consider context where users get stuck. He encourages experimentation with unexpected UI solutions rather than copying chat interfaces.
